analysis.title: End of Week Market Intelligence: conundrums
key_insights: US stocks were higher Friday 10/2 at 12:00PM and on pace for a slight weekly loss for the S&P 500 (WTD -0.3%), as investors digested a weak September payrolls report ('bad is good'), an in-line ISM Manufacturing survey, and three puzzles: rates, oil and capital markets.
September payrolls added only 29k net new jobs and the unemployment rate rose to 4.2%. GS's 3Q26 GDP tracking estimate is +3.4%, so the labor data runs weaker than the growth tracker.
GS economists pushed their October Fed funds rate hike call back to December after lower core PCE inflation. The weaker payrolls point to a less onerous path for rates.

GS economists say statistical anomalies may have depressed the September labor report. Their estimate of underlying job growth from the payroll and household surveys is 51k, roughly their estimate of the breakeven pace.

Rates puzzle: yields are rising while inflation shows signs of dissipating. Will Marshall argues the rise in bond market volatility suggests technicals and positioning may be overriding fundamentals in the move higher in rates.

Marshall says the market likely needs a catalyst to bring back duration risk appetite (push yields lower), but US valuation and positioning measures are consistent with a building asymmetry towards lower yields. GS also cites government and private-sector demand for capital as a driver of higher rates.

Oil puzzle: Yulia Grigsby estimates the global oil market is roughly balanced now, after Persian Gulf exports doubled in September to return to the 2025 level and visible global inventories stayed broadly flat. GS still worries about renewed escalation that damages more energy infrastructure, and says to watch fuel over oil.

Capital markets puzzle: IPO and M&A activity has slowed under higher rates even with stocks near all-time highs. Alex Blostein still sees a path for well-positioned private equity investors to monetize investments in the year ahead as rate pressures diminish.

AI trade: Peter Callahan says AI is becoming a stock picker's market, with the trade engaging more companies further down the value chain from pure compute power providers. Eric Sheridan's team says eCommerce is on the cusp of being reshaped by agentic AI.
Chart of the week: Alec Phillips shows gasoline prices and the Democratic generic ballot have moved together this year, so gas prices may be driving voter sentiment ahead of the midterms.
Next week's sentiment-related events are ISM Services, FOMC meeting minutes and the University of Michigan consumer confidence survey. 3Q26 earnings season starts with PEP and DAL, plus STZ and LEVI.

sector_views.rationale: Capital markets activity is held back by higher rates, though Blostein sees a path for private equity monetizations as rate pressure eases, and Financials are increasingly caught up in the AI trade.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 earnings season starts next week with PEP and DAL results due, followed by STZ and LEVI. No estimates are given.

tension_points.bull_case: Valuation and positioning measures are consistent with a building asymmetry towards lower yields, and weak payrolls with lower core PCE ease the rate path.
tension_points.bear_case: Technicals, positioning and heavy capital demand from governments and the private sector are pushing yields higher regardless of inflation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The report says the market likely needs a catalyst to bring back duration risk appetite, but does not name a specific level or event.

tension_points.bull_case: The global oil market is roughly balanced as Gulf exports recover and visible inventories stay broadly flat.
tension_points.bear_case: Renewed escalation could damage more energy infrastructure, and diesel export restrictions are a further risk.
